problem: Find the horizontal asymptote of the function $f(x)=\frac{2x+5}{2{x}^{3}+2x+6}.$

activity_context.topic_title: Limits at Infinity and Horizontal Asymptotes of Rational Functions

feedback.worked_solution:
The horizontal asymptote is $y={lim}_{x\to \infty }f(x).$ To find the horizontal asymptote, we apply the usual procedure of dividing the numerator and denominator by the highest power of $x$ in the denominator, which is ${x}^{4}.$

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to \infty }f(x) & ={lim}_{x\to \infty }\frac{18{x}^{4}+5x}{c{x}^{4}-2{x}^{3}} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to \infty }\frac{(\frac{18{x}^{4}}{{x}^{4}}+\frac{5x}{{x}^{4}})}{(\frac{c{x}^{4}}{{x}^{4}}-\frac{2{x}^{3}}{{x}^{4}})} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to \infty }\frac{(18+\frac{5}{{x}^{3}})}{(c-\frac{2}{x})} \\  & =\frac{18+0}{c-0} \\  & =\frac{18}{c}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{18}{c} & =\frac{3}{2} \\ 36 & =3c \\ c & =12.\end{aligned}
$$
